records.public_safe_text: on october 14, 2021, at approximately 8:19 p. m., i officer alcazar #[roadway] in reference to a hit and run. upon arrival to the scene, i made contact with the caller, leslie cantu who stated that her foot had been run over. leslie identified the vehicle as a 2012 black kia soul, being driver by her ex-sister-in-law, andrea sesperez. leslie stated that andrea had been looking for leslies brother, but leslie informed her that the brother was not at the residence. leslie stated that she had stepped out of her vehicle [roadway] and andrea traveled [roadway] and turned around. upon turning the vehicle around, she drove south towards leslies direction and ran over her foot before taking off. sgt isidro ybarra 601 arrived on scene and made contact with leslie, asking if she wanted to be seen by ems, to which she agreed. i was then able to observe that leslie had red marks on her left foot and the foot appeared to be swollen. sgt ybarra then asked if leslie wanted to files criminal charges against andrea, to which she responded that she did not. leslie was provided a non-prosecution affidavit and signed, declining to press criminal charges. ems unit 101 arrived to the scene, and ems technician marcos id #3275 assessed her injuries and cleared leslie.
records.redacted_narrative: on october 14, 2021, at approximately 8:19 p. m., i officer alcazar #[roadway] in reference to a hit and run. upon arrival to the scene, i made contact with the caller, leslie cantu who stated that her foot had been run over. leslie identified the vehicle as a 2012 black kia soul, being driver by her ex-sister-in-law, andrea sesperez. leslie stated that andrea had been looking for leslies brother, but leslie informed her that the brother was not at the residence. leslie stated that she had stepped out of her vehicle [roadway] and andrea traveled [roadway] and turned around. upon turning the vehicle around, she drove south towards leslies direction and ran over her foot before taking off. sgt isidro ybarra 601 arrived on scene and made contact with leslie, asking if she wanted to be seen by ems, to which she agreed. i was then able to observe that leslie had red marks on her left foot and the foot appeared to be swollen. sgt ybarra then asked if leslie wanted to files criminal charges against andrea, to which she responded that she did not. leslie was provided a non-prosecution affidavit and signed, declining to press criminal charges. ems unit 101 arrived to the scene, and ems technician marcos id #3275 assessed her injuries and cleared leslie.

records.deidentified_narrative: unit #1 was traveling south in the parking lot of london square apartment complex. unit #2, a 12 year old female pedestrian was crossing the parking lot, from her complex to her sisters parked vehicle. unit #1 stated he approached the south west corner of the parking lot, which wraps around the complex. unit #1 stated he turned left (east) in the parking lot and noticed a vehicle backed into a parking spot on the left, with it's headlights on. unit #1 stated he looked at the parked vehicle because he thought the vehicle might pull out in front of him. unit #1 stated he struck a pedestrian who was crossing the parking lot. unit #1 stated he struck the pedestrian with his front right bumper, and the pedestrian went up onto his hood and fell onto the ground. unit #1 stated he never observed the pedestrian due to it being so dark in the parking lot and no lights to illuminate the area. unit #1 stated the pedestrian was wearing a black jacket, black pants and was holding a black umbrella. the witness daisy delgado [phone] is the sister of the pedestrian (marilyn delgado) and was sitting inside of her parked vehicle, with her headlights on. daisy stated she was sitting inside of her running vehicle, [school facility]. daisy stated her sister was in the middle of the curb and her vehicle when unit #1 came around the corner and struck her. daisy stated unit #1 was not driving fast but should have been able to see the pedestrian right in front of him. daisy stated the pedestrian was struck on the left side of her body by the front right bumper of unit #1. daisy stated the pedestrian went up on the hood of unit #1 and then fell down onto the ground on the right side of her body. farmers branch medic 132 arrived on scene but the pedestrians parents refused transport. the parents of the pedestrian stated they would take her to the doctor on their own. the pedestrian had several scrapes on her right upper thigh, which were photographed and attached to the rms report [identifier].**98 may have contributed** unit #2 (pedestrian) may have attempted to cross the parking lot without looking both ways or having the umbrella she was holding in a position where it obscured her view of oncoming vehicles.

her sisters parked vehicle. unit #1 stated he approached the south west corner of the parking lot, which wraps around the complex. unit #1 stated he turned left (east) in the parking lot and noticed a vehicle backed into a parking spot on the left, with it's headlights on. unit #1 stated he looked at the parked vehicle because he thought the vehicle might pull out in front of him. unit #1 stated he struck a pedestrian who was crossing the parking lot. unit #1 stated he struck the pedestrian with his front right bumper, and the pedestrian went up onto his hood and fell onto the ground. unit #1 stated he never observed the pedestrian due to it being so dark in the parking lot and no lights to illuminate the area. unit #1 stated the pedestrian was wearing a black jacket, black pants and was holding a black umbrella. the witness daisy delgado [phone] is the sister of the pedestrian (marilyn delgado) and was sitting inside of her parked vehicle, with her headlights on. daisy stated she was sitting inside of her running vehicle, [school facility]. daisy stated her sister was in the middle of the curb and her vehicle when unit #1 came around the corner and struck her. daisy stated unit #1 was not driving fast but should have been able to see the pedestrian right in front of him. daisy stated the pedestrian was struck on the left side of her body by the front right bumper of unit #1. daisy stated the pedestrian went up on the hood of unit #1 and then fell down onto the ground on the right side of her body. farmers branch medic 132 arrived on scene but the pedestrians parents refused transport. the parents of the pedestrian stated they would take her to the doctor on their own. the pedestrian had several scrapes on her right upper thigh, which were photographed and attached to the rms report [identifier].**98 may have contributed** unit #2 (pedestrian) may have attempted to cross the parking lot without looking both ways or having the umbrella she was holding in a position where it obscured her view of oncoming vehicles.

records.deidentified_narrative: on [date] at approximately 8:19 pm, accident investigator/officer s. box #1213 was informed by rowlett dispatch of a major vehicle accident located in the 18000 block of interstate 30 west ([roadway]/[roadway]). call notes advised a pedestrian in the roadway was struck by multiple vehicles. call notes further advised the subject that was hit appeared to be a black male and appeared unconscious. accident investigator box arrived on scene at approximately 8:35 pm. upon arrival on scene, investigator box observed rowlett fire department had already arrived. upon arrival accident investigator box met with cpl. j. welk #1186. cpl. welk advised that multiple vehicles struck the pedestrian, which was located in the number 4 lane, [roadway]. cpl. welk stated it appeared pedestrian came to a rest on the white stipe divider of lanes 3 and 4. accident investigator box observed the pedestrian to be a black male laying on his back, with the top of his head facing in an eastern direction, face towards a north direction, and left arm resting against his left side, right arm facing north, left leg/foot facing southwest and right leg facing north. accident investigator box observed the victim to be wearing a black in color shirt, black in color cargo pants with a brown in color belt. cpl. welk stated the vehicles that struck the pedestrian were on scene and were parked on the shoulder west of the pedestrian. cpl. welk stated 3 other vehicles had stopped on the shoulder further along the roadway. cpl welk advised the driver of the red vehicle, parked on the shoulder, is a witness to the accident. the pedestrian struck was later identified as james lee odie (b/m 08061950). evidence collected on scene verified the identity of james along with descriptors from james' family which were reported to rowlett police department prior to the accident. james was listed as a missing person by his family with rowlett pd cfs# 21045639. the driver of the first vehicle was identified by initial responding officers as adreon cruise (w/f 01201992), the passenger was identified as james boren (w/m 07061978). the vehicle was a 2008, white in color chevrolet silverado tx-lp# [identifier] registered to james boren. adreon advised she was traveling westbound in the #4 lane and observed the victim “jump out” in front of her vehicle. adreon stated she was unable to come to a stop or change lanes to prevent from striking the victim. investigator box observed damage to the front right quarter panel, hood, and the head light on the passenger side. investigator box observed what appeared to be blood on the damaged portion of the vehicle. the driver of the second vehicle was identified as michael johnson (b/m 07211969) and passenger della johnson (b/f 11011976) who were in a 2014 white in color chevrolet silverado tx-lp# b53fz. michael stated he was unsure of what the vehicle in front of him hit (adreon's vehicle) but attempted to “straddle” it. michael stated he immediately pulled over and came to a stop. investigator box was unable to observe any damage to the front of michaels vehicle while on scene. the driver of the third vehicle was identified as anthony cordova (w/m 01301986) who was driving a 2003 white in color chevrolet tahoe tx-lp# [identifier]. anthony stated he observed the vehicles ahead of him stopping and pulling over. anthoney stated he observed the victim in the roadway and was unable to maneuver quick enough to keep from hitting the victim. investigator box did not observe damage to the front end of anthony's vehicle while on scene. while interviewing all subjects listed above, all subjects stated they were unable to avoid hitting the victim and immediately stopped upon realizing what happened. a fourth vehicle on scene stopped as a witness to the accident. the driver/witness was identified as sierra king (b/f 09041999) who was driving a 2010 red in color ford fusion tx-lp #[identifier]. sierra [roadway] #1 and observed the victim get hit by the vehicles. sierra stated it appeared as the victim was going to [roadway] in the attempt of crossing it. investigator box completed tow sheets for all 3 chevrolet's and placed an investigative hold on the vehicles. sierra was released from the scene after her vehicle was cleared and appeared there was no evidence showing she was involved in the accident other than a witness. accident investigator box walked the scene of the accident and observed a left and right shoe belonging to the victim, black in color. the right shoe was located first in the # 4 lane just west of the entrance ramp from dalrock to i30 west. the left shoe [roadway] #4. clear plastic pieces believed to be from the vehicle, were found in the # 4 lane and shoulder, within close proximity of the shoes. further west from the clear plastic pieces a “army” [roadway] #3. a black in color cell phone with damage was located on the shoulder close to the jersey barrier. a white in color phone charger was located between lanes #1 and #2. [roadway] of blood stain from the victim was observed between the #3 and #4 lanes running west along the white stripes that divide the lanes. accident investigator box was unable to locate any other roadway evidence at the time and no measurements were taken. the area of the accident did not have a pedestrian cross walk and was poorly lit. the outside temperature was approximately 62 degrees fahrenheit, and it was dark outside. evidence was marked with orange paint by officer t. paxton # 1198. the evidence was collected by officer m. davison # 1182 and placed into rowlett property and evidence located at [roadway]., rowlett. officer davison took photographs of the scene and attached them to the report. the victim was pronounced deceased on [date] at approximately 8:30 pm by dallas county medical examiner h. pena who arrived on scene at approximately 12:01 am ([date]). pena informed accident investigator box the time of death was based upon the time rowlett fire department arrived on scene and knew they would not be able to perform life saving measures on the victim due to injuries sustained and it was clear the victim was deceased. pena advised and autopsy would be performed the following morning. at the time of this report, the results are pending and unknown. pena stated the report number for this case with dallas county medical examiner officer is ifs-21-22316. the following information was received the following day of the crash:on [date] at 5:31 pm, officer s. box received a phone call from lindsay sowden (w/f 12301981) who advised she thinks she was involved in the crash that occurred on i30. lindsay stated she was [roadway]., (time and date of initial call), and observed several people who had stopped on the shoulder. lindsay believed it was caused by a wreck and stated she observed possibly a ""body"" in the roadway. lindsay stated she was in her gray 2012 infinity qx5 (suv) tx lp: [identifier] at the time of the accident. lindsay said she did not hit/run over the victim and was able to avoid any other vehicles that were stopped on/in the roadway. while attempting to get though traffic from the accident, lindsay stated she was almost certain she observed blood in the roadway and believed she had drove through it, while in the #4 lane, due to not being able to change lanes. lindsay advise she was not traveling at a high rate of speed and had slowed down at this time. lindsay informed officer box, the following morning after driving through the area of the crash, her dog was outside and began to sniff the front right fender of her vehicle. upon further examination, lindsay observed what appeared to be small red dots along the inner fender of the front right portion of the vehicle. lindsay stated at this time she believed it was possibly blood from the victim. lindsay informed her husband of her findings on the vehicle and thought best to contact rowlett pd in regards to the incident. while speaking with lindsay via phone, officer box asked if she could email pictures due to the vehicle being [roadway] of residence, also to protect the potential loss of any evidence being destroyed while en route back to rowlett pd. officer box instructed lindsay not to wash or attempt to clean the vehicle unit pictures were received and observed by officer box. upon receiving photos of lindsay's vehicle, officer box determined it was not of any evidentiary value to the case due to the minimal transfer and no signs of damage on the vehicle. officer box believes the blood was transferred on to the vehicle from the roadway and not the victim.

records.public_safe_text: on [date] at approximately 8:19 pm, accident investigator/officer s. box #1213 was informed by rowlett dispatch of a major vehicle accident located in the 18000 block of interstate 30 west ([roadway]/[roadway]). call notes advised a pedestrian in the roadway was struck by multiple vehicles. call notes further advised the subject that was hit appeared to be a black male and appeared unconscious. accident investigator box arrived on scene at approximately 8:35 pm. upon arrival on scene, investigator box observed rowlett fire department had already arrived. upon arrival accident investigator box met with cpl. j. welk #1186. cpl. welk advised that multiple vehicles struck the pedestrian, which was located in the number 4 lane, [roadway]. cpl. welk stated it appeared pedestrian came to a rest on the white stipe divider of lanes 3 and 4. accident investigator box observed the pedestrian to be a black male laying on his back, with the top of his head facing in an eastern direction, face towards a north direction, and left arm resting against his left side, right arm facing north, left leg/foot facing southwest and right leg facing north. accident investigator box observed the victim to be wearing a black in color shirt, black in color cargo pants with a brown in color belt. cpl. welk stated the vehicles that struck the pedestrian were on scene and were parked on the shoulder west of the pedestrian. cpl. welk stated 3 other vehicles had stopped on the shoulder further along the roadway. cpl welk advised the driver of the red vehicle, parked on the shoulder, is a witness to the accident. the pedestrian struck was later identified as james lee odie (b/m 08061950). evidence collected on scene verified the identity of james along with descriptors from james' family which were reported to rowlett police department prior to the accident. james was listed as a missing person by his family with rowlett pd cfs# 21045639. the driver of the first vehicle was identified by initial responding officers as adreon cruise (w/f 01201992), the passenger was identified as james boren (w/m 07061978). the vehicle was a 2008, white in color chevrolet silverado tx-lp# [identifier] registered to james boren. adreon advised she was traveling westbound in the #4 lane and observed the victim “jump out” in front of her vehicle. adreon stated she was unable to come to a stop or change lanes to prevent from striking the victim. investigator box observed damage to the front right quarter panel, hood, and the head light on the passenger side. investigator box observed what appeared to be blood on the damaged portion of the vehicle. the driver of the second vehicle was identified as michael johnson (b/m 07211969) and passenger della johnson (b/f 11011976) who were in a 2014 white in color chevrolet silverado tx-lp# b53fz. michael stated he was unsure of what the vehicle in front of him hit (adreon's vehicle) but attempted to “straddle” it. michael stated he immediately pulled over and came to a stop. investigator box was unable to observe any damage to the front of michaels vehicle while on scene. the driver of the third vehicle was identified as anthony cordova (w/m 01301986) who was driving a 2003 white in color chevrolet tahoe tx-lp# [identifier]. anthony stated he observed the vehicles ahead of him stopping and pulling over. anthoney stated he observed the victim in the roadway and was unable to maneuver quick enough to keep from hitting the victim. investigator box did not observe damage to the front end of anthony's vehicle while on scene. while interviewing all subjects listed above, all subjects stated they were unable to avoid hitting the victim and immediately stopped upon realizing what happened. a fourth vehicle on scene stopped as a witness to the accident. the driver/witness was identified as sierra king (b/f 09041999) who was driving a 2010 red in color ford fusion tx-lp #[identifier]. sierra [roadway] #1 and observed the victim get hit by the vehicles. sierra stated it appeared as the victim was going to [roadway] in the attempt of crossing it. investigator box completed tow sheets for all 3 chevrolet's and placed an investigative hold on the vehicles. sierra was released from the scene after her vehicle was cleared and appeared there was no evidence showing she was involved in the accident other than a witness. accident investigator box walked the scene of the accident and observed a left and right shoe belonging to the victim, black in color. the right shoe was located first in the # 4 lane just west of the entrance ramp from dalrock to i30 west. the left shoe [roadway] #4. clear plastic pieces believed to be from the vehicle, were found in the # 4 lane and shoulder, within close proximity of the shoes. further west from the clear plastic pieces a “army” [roadway] #3. a black in color cell phone with damage was located on the shoulder close to the jersey barrier. a white in color phone charger was located between lanes #1 and #2. [roadway] of blood stain from the victim was observed between the #3 and #4 lanes running west along the white stripes that divide the lanes. accident investigator box was unable to locate any other roadway evidence at the time and no measurements were taken. the area of the accident did not have a pedestrian cross walk and was poorly lit. the outside temperature was approximately 62 degrees fahrenheit, and it was dark outside. evidence was marked with orange paint by officer t. paxton # 1198. the evidence was collected by officer m. davison # 1182 and placed into rowlett property and evidence located at [roadway]., rowlett. officer davison took photographs of the scene and attached them to the report. the victim was pronounced deceased on [date] at approximately 8:30 pm by dallas county medical examiner h. pena who arrived on scene at approximately 12:01 am ([date]). pena informed accident investigator box the time of death was based upon the time rowlett fire department arrived on scene and knew they would not be able to perform life saving measures on the victim due to injuries sustained and it was clear the victim was deceased. pena advised and autopsy would be performed the following morning. at the time of this report, the results are pending and unknown. pena stated the report number for this case with dallas county medical examiner officer is ifs-21-22316. the following information was received the following day of the crash:on [date] at 5:31 pm, officer s. box received a phone call from lindsay sowden (w/f 12301981) who advised she thinks she was involved in the crash that occurred on i30. lindsay stated she was [roadway]., (time and date of initial call), and observed several people who had stopped on the shoulder. lindsay believed it was caused by a wreck and stated she observed possibly a ""body"" in the roadway. lindsay stated she was in her gray 2012 infinity qx5 (suv) tx lp: [identifier] at the time of the accident. lindsay said she did not hit/run over the victim and was able to avoid any other vehicles that were stopped on/in the roadway. while attempting to get though traffic from the accident, lindsay stated she was almost certain she observed blood in the roadway and believed she had drove through it, while in the #4 lane, due to not being able to change lanes. lindsay advise she was not traveling at a high rate of speed and had slowed down at this time. lindsay informed officer box, the following morning after driving through the area of the crash, her dog was outside and began to sniff the front right fender of her vehicle. upon further examination, lindsay observed what appeared to be small red dots along the inner fender of the front right portion of the vehicle. lindsay stated at this time she believed it was possibly blood from the victim. lindsay informed her husband of her findings on the vehicle and thought best to contact rowlett pd in regards to the incident. while speaking with lindsay via phone, officer box asked if she could email pictures due to the vehicle being [roadway] of residence, also to protect the potential loss of any evidence being destroyed while en route back to rowlett pd. officer box instructed lindsay not to wash or attempt to clean the vehicle unit pictures were received and observed by officer box. upon receiving photos of lindsay's vehicle, officer box determined it was not of any evidentiary value to the case due to the minimal transfer and no signs of damage on the vehicle. officer box believes the blood was transferred on to the vehicle from the roadway and not the victim.
